newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says Egypt order could be extended.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says Egypt order could be extended.

text.p: British aero-engine maker Rolls-Royce said on Sunday it hoped a deal worth up to $450 million with the private Kato Group of Egypt for engines to power Russian Tupolev airliners would be followed by more.
But a Rolls-Royce spokesman said a Sunday Times report saying the company was "poised" for orders from Kato worth two billion pounds ($3.1 billion) was the newspaper's own inference.
"If the Kato group eventually orders 200 aircraft, it could be worth that," the spokesman said.
Under the deal already announced last Thursday, Kato ordered engines for 13 aircraft and took options on another 17.
"We are delighted to have landed the programme and will be waiting to hear more from the Kato Group," the spokesman said.

Rolls disappointed investors on Thursday by leaving its interim dividend unchanged as it reported a first-half loss of 169 million pounds. The loss was due to one-off charges relating from Rolls' withdrawal from steam power generation and was anticipated by equities markets.

But the company is also expected to benefit from a major defence deal with Qatar, which industry watchers say could be one of the orders due to be unveiled this week at the Farnborough air show in England.
